candidate_interpretation: Fires on mentions of multi-subunit molecular machines / complexes in DNA biology (e.g. eIF3, RNA polymerase II core, CMG helicase, clamp loaders, POLE, 40S ribosomal subunit scanning) -- specifically around the naming/description of a named macromolecular complex and its mechanistic role, concentrated in Transcription_Translation and Replication subdomains.
evidence_supporting: Discovery top-8 examples are all DNA Transcription_Translation/Replication prompts naming specific multi-subunit complexes (eIF3, RNA Pol II core, DNA pol alpha-primase, Cdc45/GINS, tau subunit of Pol III). 31 Tier-1 confirmed template families in Discovery and 33 in Confirmation (not just Tier-3 noise), spanning 39 subdomains. Confirmation top examples independently surface the same theme without overlap with Discovery examples (POLE catalytic subunit, 40S subunit scanning, GTFs assembling at promoter, ATM kinase dimer, DnaA-box initiator complex, dominant-negative multimeric protein). same_concept_different_template counterexamples mostly fired (40S subunit scanning, POLE structural feature) confirming generalization across phrasing.
evidence_contradicting: domain_concentration and cross_domain_entropy are consistent discovery vs confirmation, but script_language_score shows a large_divergence flag (0.15 -> 0.25), meaning a modest but growing minority of firings are on HINDI/SCIENCE prompts unrelated to DNA complexes -- not fully clean. One same_concept_different_template counterexample (chromatin structure influencing RNAP access) did not fire, and one different_domain_same_surface_form SCIENCE ribosome-stall prompt also did not fire despite plausible conceptual overlap, showing the feature is not simply 'any multi-subunit-complex concept' generically.
domain_dependence: Applied the domain-specific framing: DNA is the home domain (826/958 Discovery firings, 767/916 Confirmation firings), so concentration there is expected and not penalized. Within DNA the feature shows real internal diversity -- 39 distinct subdomains touched in Discovery, 31 Tier-1 confirmed template families (not merely Tier-3 unclustered), and topics span replication, transcription, translation, and repair machinery rather than one recurring phrasing.
script_language_dependence: Not a script/language-dependent feature -- almost all firing mass is on English DNA-domain text; the small HINDI/SCIENCE residual (script_language_score ~0.15-0.25) does not track meaning and is noted as a minor contaminant rather than the feature's basis.
potential_polysemanticity: Looks like one coherent concept (named multi-subunit molecular machines in DNA biology) rather than multiple unrelated bundled concepts; no examples suggest a second unrelated theme.

candidate_interpretation: Fires on physics/physical-science causal-mechanism reasoning prompts -- i.e. text describing a physical system or phenomenon (projectile motion, induction, turbulence, thermal expansion, orbital motion, corrosion) phrased as 'trace the causal chain', 'explain the mechanism', 'reason through X using <subfield>' -- concentrated in SCIENCE subdomains Mechanics/Electromagnetism/Fluid mechanics/Thermodynamics/Optics/Astrophysics/Electrochemistry.
evidence_supporting: Discovery top-8 and one_per_template examples span 7+ distinct physics subdomains (Mechanics, Electromagnetism, Astrophysics, Fluid mechanics, Thermodynamics, Optics) with 91 Tier-1 confirmed template families (not Tier-3 noise) and 68 subdomains touched. Confirmation independently reproduces the same pattern (96 Tier-1 families, same physics subdomains: Thermodynamics gas cooling, Electromagnetism charged particle, Mechanics bridge vibration, Electrochemistry metal corrosion) with consistent domain_concentration (2.81 discovery vs 2.81 confirmation) and cross_domain_entropy (0.69 vs 0.67). same_concept_different_template counterexamples (Astrophysics gravitational lensing, galaxy rotation curve, Electrochemistry internal resistance) mostly fired, showing generalization beyond the exact top templates.
evidence_contradicting: The feature is not purely physics-specific: secondary firing occurs in DNA, HINDI, EMOTIONS, GANDHI at lower activation (mid-tier examples include Hindi grammar, DNA mismatch repair, emotional comparison prompts), so it may partly be a generic 'contrastive/causal reasoning template' marker rather than physics-content-specific. prelim_cross_seed_pass_discovery_only is false, a caveat not to be weighted here but noted.
domain_dependence: Applied domain-specific framing: SCIENCE is the dominant firing domain (1361/2196 discovery, 1435/2270 confirmation), with high internal diversity across many physics subfields (Mechanics, EM, Thermo, Fluid, Optics, Astrophysics, Electrochemistry) rather than one recurring template -- 91-96 Tier-1 confirmed families support real within-domain diversity, not just one phrasing.
script_language_dependence: Not script-dependent; script_language_score is low-moderate (0.24-0.27) and firing is concentrated on English physics text, so this is not a Hindi-script marker.
potential_polysemanticity: Mostly one coherent concept (physics causal/mechanistic reasoning), though the lower-activation tail touching non-physics domains (grammar, emotion comparisons) suggests a secondary, weaker generic-reasoning-template component bundled in at low activation.

candidate_interpretation: Hindi-script/language marker -- fires broadly across Hindi-language text regardless of topic (grammar, syntax, semantics, pragmatics, vocabulary), not on a specific semantic concept.
evidence_supporting: HINDI is overwhelmingly the dominant domain (1907/2317 = 82% of Discovery firings, 1835/2194 = 84% of Confirmation firings), consistent across subset splits. evidence_contradicting: Not a pure script marker either: 73-123 firings occur in GANDHI/SCIENCE/EMOTIONS/DNA (English) each subset, and four of five same_concept_different_template counterexamples on Hindi content fired at meaningfully varying activations (0.07-0.45) rather than uniformly, suggesting some sensitivity to content/position within Hindi text, not pure language-identity.
domain_dependence: Applied the cross-domain/general-candidate framing since the feature spans many unrelated subdomains within HINDI (109 subdomains in Discovery) with no topical theme; this broad, topic-independent spread within the dominant language is itself evidence against a semantic-concept interpretation and supports a language-marker interpretation.
script_language_dependence: Fires on Hindi-script content largely independent of meaning -- examples span grammar, idiom, pragmatics, and semantics questions with no shared topic, and firing tracks the presence of Devanagari/Hindi text rather than any specific meaning within it.
potential_polysemanticity: Appears to be a single broad language/script-detection mechanism rather than multiple distinct bundled concepts, though activation magnitude varies with position/content in ways not fully explained.

candidate_interpretation: Primarily tracks Hindi lexical-semantic contrast/definition prompts (e.g. distinguishing near-synonym word pairs like 'अपेक्षा/उपेक्षा', 'सम्मान/आदर', 'क्षणिक/स्थायी'), heavily concentrated in HINDI Semantics/Vocabulary/Grammar subdomains, but with substantial leakage onto unrelated Hindi-script content.
short_label: Hindi word-meaning contrast feature (with script leakage)
evidence_supporting: HINDI dominates firing (1970/2100 = 94% discovery, 1888/2021 = 93% confirmation, consistent across splits). Top activating examples in both Discovery and Confirmation are overwhelmingly word-pair semantic-contrast or single-word meaning questions (e.g. 'मूल्य कर सहित' vs 'कर अतिरिक्त', 'सम्मान'/'आदर', 'क्षणिक'/'स्थायी', 'प्रभाव'/'परिणाम'). 46-49 Tier-1 confirmed template families support this being more than coincidence.
evidence_contradicting: same_script_unrelated_semantics counterexamples fired at substantial activation (0.12-0.34) on Hindi syntax/pragmatics prompts with no word-contrast content (e.g. noun-phrase identification, turn-taking pragmatics), which is roughly half the magnitude of the top word-contrast activations (0.65-0.83) -- meaning (as the task defines it) this is NOT clean evidence for a semantic, non-marker interpretation; the feature partially fires on unrelated same-script material.
domain_dependence: Applied domain-specific framing (home domain HINDI): within-domain diversity is real (36-44 subdomains, 46-49 Tier-1 families spanning different word pairs), but the domain concentration itself (HINDI ~94%) combined with notable same-script-unrelated-semantics firing argues the underlying driver may be partly script-level rather than purely the semantic contrast concept.
script_language_dependence: Tested against same_script_unrelated_semantics counterexamples: activation does NOT cleanly track meaning -- it fires at meaningfully high levels (0.12-0.34) on unrelated same-script pragmatics/syntax content, well above the mid-tier threshold (~0.10) and not negligible relative to top activations, so this leans toward a script/language-flavored marker rather than a cleanly semantic concept, despite the strong lexical-contrast signal at the very top of the activation distribution.
potential_polysemanticity: Likely polysemantic/mixed: a genuine lexical-semantic-contrast sub-signal at highest activations bundled with a broader Hindi-script-sensitivity component that fires on unrelated content at lower-but-still-meaningful activation.

candidate_interpretation: No coherent single concept identifiable -- this is the experiment's own 'cross_seed_prescreened_nonreproducible_control' feature, and the evidence matches that label: very high cross-domain entropy with firing spread roughly evenly across all five unrelated domains and no shared topic among top examples.
short_label: Nonreproducible control feature, no coherent theme

domain_dependence: Applied the cross-domain/general-candidate framing since the feature is explicitly a broadly-distributed control: very low domain concentration (1.32-1.47) and near-maximal cross-domain entropy support that it is NOT a coherent domain-specific signal, consistent with the 'nonreproducible_control' label.
script_language_dependence: Not a script/language marker -- script_language_score is low (1.28-1.66) and firing is not concentrated on Hindi-script content specifically relative to its broad multi-domain spread.
potential_polysemanticity: If anything is 'bundled' here it looks like multiple unrelated, weak triggers rather than one concept -- consistent with this being a designed negative control rather than a genuine feature with a semantic story.

evidence_supporting: DNA dominates firing (1096/2529 discovery, 961/2443 confirmation) with Inheritance_Genomics as the dominant subdomain in nearly all top examples (GWAS design, 16S rRNA vs shotgun metagenomics, adapter trimming, synteny analysis, contamination detection, whole-genome sequencing of trios). 91-100 Tier-1 confirmed template families (not Tier-3 noise) support genuine generalization. Confirmation independently reproduces the same topic cluster (population stratification in GWAS, Hi-C scaffolding, eQTLs, QTL vs GWAS loci) with consistent domain_concentration (3.82 vs 3.45) -- same_concept_different_template counterexamples (Hi-C scaffolding, sequencing depth, population stratification, satellite DNA repeat classification) all fired, showing solid generalization across phrasing.
evidence_contradicting: cross_domain_entropy_norm is fairly high (0.83-0.86) because SCIENCE also fires substantially (772/2529 discovery) on topically adjacent but not identical content (molecular/evolutionary biology mechanism questions), and EMOTIONS fires non-trivially too (351-478), including on an emotion-lexicon/cross-lingual-recognition question that is only loosely genomics-adjacent (shares 'methodology/measurement' framing, not genomics content) -- suggesting the feature may partly key on a 'methodology/measurement design' framing rather than genomics content alone.
domain_dependence: Applied domain-specific framing (home domain DNA, ~43% of firings): within-domain diversity is strong -- Inheritance_Genomics dominates but the feature also touches Transcription_Translation (ChIP-seq) and Replication (bacterial vs eukaryotic genome organization), across 91-100 Tier-1 confirmed families, supporting a real methodological concept rather than one template.
script_language_dependence: Not script-dependent; script_language_score is very low (0.14) and stable, firing is concentrated on English genomics-methodology text.
potential_polysemanticity: Mostly one coherent concept (genomics/sequencing methodology), with a secondary weaker 'general scientific methodology/measurement' tendency visible in the SCIENCE and EMOTIONS firings that is topically adjacent but not genomics-specific -- a mild polysemantic lean worth flagging.

candidate_interpretation: Fires on the fixed collocation 'organizational method' appearing at a specific token position within several recurring GANDHI prompt templates ('Construct a causal explanation linking X and organizational method...', 'Develop a public-facing exhibit... around X and organizational method...', 'How does understanding organizational method change the interpretation of X?'), where X (the historical topic) varies freely -- a template/phrase-position trigger rather than a concept about the varying topics themselves.
evidence_supporting: Virtually all of the highest activations (2.0-2.26) are GANDHI prompts containing the literal phrase 'organizational method', with the variable topic X ranging freely across unrelated subjects (Technology and modernity, Natal Indian Congress, Religious influences, Kheda, Untouchability, Round Table Conference) -- the invariant element is the fixed phrase/token position, not the topic. template_diversity has 83/80 Tier-1 confirmed families purely because many distinct 'X' topics are slotted into the same small set of fixed sentence frames.
evidence_contradicting: Firing is not perfectly template-locked: mid-tier Discovery/Confirmation examples include unrelated EMOTIONS, SCIENCE, and HINDI prompts with no 'organizational method' phrase at much lower activation, and different_domain_same_surface_form SCIENCE counterexamples (material fracture surface) fired at moderate activation (0.32) despite no such phrase, which is some evidence against pure phrase-matching.
domain_dependence: The selection's own primary_stratum is 'cross_domain_broadly_distributed' and cross_domain_entropy_norm is near-maximal (0.99, stable), but this reflects the fixed phrase being slotted into many different topic templates within GANDHI, not genuine cross-domain conceptual generalization -- applying the cross-domain framing, the low domain concentration is actually explained by template mechanics rather than a broad semantic concept.
script_language_dependence: Not a script/language feature; firing is on English text and script_language_score (1.2-1.3) is unremarkable.
potential_polysemanticity: Appears to be a single phrase/position detector with a low-activation noise floor across unrelated domains, not a bundle of distinct semantic concepts.

potential_polysemanticity: Primarily a single phrase/position detector; the diffuse low-activation cross-domain tail is weak noise rather than a second coherent concept.

candidate_interpretation: Fires at a fixed early token position (position 4) on the recurring question-opener 'What is the role of ...' within DNA-domain prompts, regardless of which specific molecular entity or mechanism follows -- a syntactic template-position trigger rather than a concept about DNA content.
short_label: 'What is the role of' template-position trigger (DNA)
evidence_supporting: All of the strongest activations (0.91-0.92) occur at token_position 4 across structurally identical 'What is the role of [X] in [Y]?' openers spanning many unrelated DNA mechanisms (NER in cisplatin crosslink repair, UV-DDB complex, water bridges in base pairs, nucleosome-depleted regions, polymerase theta, cGAS-STING, BRD4). Confirmation reproduces the exact same activation values (0.91-0.91) at the same token position on entirely new topics (centromere, XRN2, MutH, counterions, topoisomerase), strongly supporting a position/phrase-locked trigger that generalizes across DNA sub-content.
evidence_contradicting: The very high domain_concentration (8.56 discovery) drops sharply in Confirmation (6.48) with a large_divergence flag on cross_domain_entropy_norm (0.08 -> 0.36), and 11/42 Confirmation firings are now EMOTIONS prompts using the same 'What is the role of' phrasing -- confirming this is a phrase-position trigger that is not DNA-specific at all, just DNA-dominant in this corpus because that phrasing happens to be common there. n_firing_tokens is very small (34 discovery, 42 confirmation).
domain_dependence: Applied domain-specific framing initially (DNA is 33/34 discovery firings) but the Confirmation divergence (EMOTIONS prompts now firing on the same phrase) shows the apparent domain concentration is an artifact of phrase frequency in the DNA portion of the corpus, not a genuine DNA concept -- this undermines the domain-specific story rather than supporting it.
script_language_dependence: Not script-dependent; script_language_score is 0 throughout, firing is purely on the English phrase 'What is the role of' at a fixed position.
potential_polysemanticity: Single mechanism (fixed phrase/position detector) rather than multiple concepts, but its cross-domain reproducibility (DNA and EMOTIONS both trigger it in Confirmation) argues against calling it 'domain-specific' at all.

domain_dependence: Selection's primary_stratum is 'cross_domain_broadly_distributed' with near-maximal cross_domain_entropy_norm (0.99), but this reflects firing on a fixed phrase that happens to recur heavily within GANDHI-domain templates (41/230 and 36/248 Tier-1 confirmed families largely reflect the one template family with varying X) rather than a genuine cross-domain semantic concept.
script_language_dependence: Not primarily script-dependent; the instability (large_divergence) in script_language_score suggests the low-activation tail is noisy, but the dominant driver is the fixed English phrase at a fixed position, not Hindi script.
potential_polysemanticity: Primarily a single phrase/position detector; the diffuse cross-domain low-activation tail looks like unrelated noise rather than a second coherent concept.
